finding: Protocol-clean (unmasked) numbers are far below the masked diagnostics: blend HR@10 0.0484 test vs 0.0751 masked — history items occupy top ranks when not masked. The blend's win over content largely EVAPORATES on test at @10 (0.0484 vs 0.0475, +0.0009) and INVERTS at @5 (0.0175 vs 0.0234): collab z-scores push recently-bought history items into the top-5. On val the blend still wins clearly (0.0645 vs 0.0497 HR@10), but val histories = the very train prefixes the collab space was built on — distribution match, not generalization. Residual region probes DO beat pure dense at early precision on test: K4 HR@5 0.0243 / NDCG@5 0.0120 vs blend 0.0175/0.0079 and vs content 0.0234/0.0115 (best NDCG@5 of all training-free methods), at mean candidate budget 89 (K4) vs 20/50 budget-matched controls which are identical to blend by construction. No residual K beats blend at HR@10 (max 0.0443 vs 0.0484). Cold items (n=162): blend and residual score 0.0 (cold items have no collab vector, z-blend buries them) while content-only gets 0.0617 — any collab-blended method needs a content fallback for cold. External bars (verified hit ~0.068, NDCG@5 0.0486) remain far above ALL training-free methods; a trained model (J2) is required.

summary: Residual greedy-region ORACLE at matched budget, protocol-clean (fit on val, one test report). Oracle candidate recall 0.687 test / 0.695 val at K=1 already (target sits in its OWN region's top-20 list 69% of the time) vs matched dense top-M recall 0.135 (M=35) .. 0.236 (M=105). Recall headroom vs budget-matched dense: +0.45..+0.55 ABSOLUTE. BUT: blend-score re-ranking of the union changes HR@10/NDCG@5 by EXACTLY 0.0 (structural: every region-added candidate scores below the dense top-20 under the same blend score, asserted).
gate_verdict: A1/RGRP gate FAILS as originally specified (+0.010 HR at matched budget under blend re-rank = structurally impossible), but the FINDING is that the gate metric was degenerate, not that regions are useless: regions are a superb CANDIDATE GENERATOR (0.687 recall upper bound vs 0.0487 dense HR@10) that cannot be converted by the same dense score that failed to rank the target. CONDITIONAL PASS: A1/RGRP proceeds ONLY coupled with a trained union re-ranker (A3/LDRR or C4 calibrated fusion).
findings: Strongest pro-region evidence to date, but at the candidate level: region lists concentrate the target far better than deeper dense lists at equal budget

The binding constraints are now (a) region PREDICTION (planner: realistic hit@K ~0.19-0.25 from C2, x0.687 conversion ceiling) and (b) union RE-RANKING (a scorer that can promote region candidates past dense false positives)

Re-prioritization: A3/LDRR and C4 calibrated fusion move UP, ahead of RGRP; P3 union ranking oracle becomes the critical next gate and must use REALISTIC predictor unions (knn top-K regions), not oracle regions

summary: Candidate-union RANKING oracle + learnability probe on REALISTIC unions (dense blend top-20 U top-20 lists of top-K knn-soft-vote predicted regions, K in {1,3,5}; VOTE_TOP=200, P2 content-fallback). Protocol-clean: fit on VAL 80%, model/K chosen on VAL 20% holdout, single TEST report per config. (a) REALISTIC union recall (test): 0.113 (K1, size ~35) / 0.154 (K3, ~70) / 0.184 (K5, ~107) - BELOW budget-matched dense top-M recall (0.135/0.196/0.236): with the realistic predictor the region union LOSES the P2 oracle recall advantage (0.687 was oracle-only). (b) Ranking-oracle upper bound = union recall; gap vs dense HR@10 0.0487: +0.064/+0.105/+0.136 test. (c) LEARNABILITY: a 17-feature HistGradientBoosting re-ranker CONVERTS most of it - test HR@10 0.0722 (K1) / 0.0769 (K3) / 0.0784 (K5) and NDCG@5 0.0316/0.0324/0.0322 vs dense blend 0.0487/0.0079; even plain logistic regression passes (HR@10 0.061-0.062, NDCG@5 0.018-0.019). Conversion efficiency HGB: HR@10/union-recall ~0.64 (K1) to 0.43 (K5). Ablation (val-holdout NDCG@5, HGB, K1): rank-only 0.0295 -> +scores 0.0345 -> +region/meta 0.0445; top LR |coef|: log_pop 0.36, same_brand 0.31, blend_s 0.30, dense_rank 0.26, collab_z 0.26. Cold items (n=162) get WORSE under the re-ranker (HR@10 0.006-0.031 vs blend 0.049): popularity feature buries them.
gate_verdict: GATE PASSES - ALL 6 (model,K) configs clear both thresholds (needed +0.010 HR@10 or +0.004 NDCG@5). Primary (val-holdout pick): K=1 HGB, test HR@10 0.0722 (+0.0235), NDCG@5 0.0316 (+0.0237). Best any-K: K=5 HGB HR@10 0.0784 (+0.0297). Also beats P1 content-only reference (NDCG@5 0.0115, HR@10 0.0475) by ~2.8x NDCG@5. Test HR@10 0.0784 even exceeds the external trained-model verified hit bar (~0.068), though NDCG@5 0.032 is still below the external 0.0486. LDRR PROCEEDS; RGRP conditionally proceeds as candidate generator + LDRR re-ranker.
findings: Learnability confirmed decisively: simple inference-time features (popularity, same-brand-as-last, blend score, dense rank, collab z) separate the target from union false positives; even LR passes the gate, HGB roughly quadruples blend NDCG@5

IMPORTANT CAVEAT: realistic-predictor unions have LOWER candidate recall than budget-matched dense top-M at every K - the gain is coming from the LEARNED RE-RANKER, not from region candidates per se. The missing control is the same HGB re-ranking dense top-M (M=35/70/107) candidates; region value-add is NOT yet demonstrated at the candidate level under realistic prediction
Region/meta features carry real signal for RANKING even if region lists don't add recall: ablation +region/meta adds +0.010 val NDCG@5 over rank+scores (0.0345 -> 0.0445)
